page: Microsoft Azure D160ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 80 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 640.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 9449 GB of NVMe SSD capacity and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench metrics. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 14521.33 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 464.15 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI. The system also demonstrates top-tier performance in database operations, processing 204.26 million Redis SET operations per second, and achieves high throughput in static web serving and multi-threaded decompression. Large-model LLM inference benchmarks show strong to top-tier performance, processing 37.48 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model.

Given its high resource density, the server offers qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise deployments by consolidating massive compute, memory, and local NVMe storage into a single virtualized footprint. The lack of a dedicated GPU represents a tradeoff for machine learning training, but the high vCPU count and fast memory bandwidth make it highly capable for CPU-based LLM inference. This server is optimized for demanding workloads such as large relational databases, high-throughput Redis caching layers, heavy web serving, software compilation, and data-intensive enterprise applications.
